plan.estimand: Between-group main effect in repeated-measures ANOVA (difference in average response across 3 repeated measures)
plan.hypothesis: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ vs H₁: μ₁ ≠ μ₂, where μ₁ and μ₂ are the group means of subject-level averages across repeated measurements
assumptions: Multivariate normal observations within each group
Compound symmetry covariance structure (common within-subject correlation 0.5 across all pairs of occasions)
Equal variances across groups (homogeneity of variance)
Between-group analysis performed on subject-level averages (simplification of the full repeated-measures model)
scientific_notes: The between-group F test (equivalently, pooled t test on subject-level averages) ignores the within-subject correlation structure and treats the 3-occasion average as the outcome for each participant.

Under compound symmetry with correlation ρ=0.5, the variance of the subject-level average is Var(mean across k occasions) = σ²[(1 - ρ)/k + ρ], where σ is the marginal SD. With k=3 and σ=2.5, this yields Var(average) = 2.5² × [(1 - 0.5)/3 + 0.5] ≈ 6.25 × (0.1667 + 0.5) = 6.25 × 0.6667 ≈ 4.167, so SD(average) ≈ 2.041.

The effect size (group 1 mean − group 2 mean) = 51 − 49 = 2 on the scale of individual observations, which becomes Cohen's d = 2 / √(2 × 4.167) ≈ 2 / 2.887 ≈ 0.692 on the scale of subject-level averages.

This is a post-hoc power calculation for a specified design once the minimum integer sample size achieving 80% power is identified, and verification will confirm achieved power at the selected and preceding designs.
